scoring_note: Editorial musical hypotheses, not calibrated listeners. Specialist lane is proposed/inactive until routing and catalog activation are separately approved.

songs.title: Peg
songs.rationale: Pristine ensemble precision with a watchful perspective; a sophisticated foil for soft-focus solitude.

songs.title: Sailing
songs.rationale: Weightless private escape, all atmosphere and patient drift rather than command or rhythmic insistence.

songs.title: Rosanna
songs.rationale: A muscular, immaculate studio groove with a big communal chorus, showing how refined playing can still push.

songs.title: What a Fool Believes
songs.rationale: A buoyant arrangement conceals romantic self-deception: seemingly frictionless sound, emotionally complicated story.

songs.title: I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near)
songs.rationale: The bass-driven groove commands the body while the lyric stays stuck in emotional denial.

songs.title: Lowdown
songs.rationale: Slick, judgmental funk that rewards an assertive, observational stance over tender vulnerability.

songs.title: Baby Come Back
songs.rationale: A polished but exposed plea that sets confidence aside to live inside unresolved longing.

songs.title: Reminiscing
songs.rationale: Harmonies and nostalgia turn a private romantic memory into an expansive, effortless glide.

songs.title: Biggest Part of Me
songs.rationale: Ornate harmonies and heartfelt reassurance reward warmth and immaculate finish over lyrical distance.

songs.title: Georgy Porgy
songs.rationale: A layered, laid-back jazz-funk groove asks for patient attention rather than a decisive shout.

songs.title: This Is It
songs.rationale: An urgent life-advice anthem disguised as soft rock, with the vocalist pushing rather than floating.

songs.title: Deacon Blues
songs.rationale: An elaborate, inwardly weary narrator rewards close observation and slow accumulation over easy release.

songs.title: You Make My Dreams
songs.rationale: Sunny, immediate pop insistence tests the appetite for public joy over patient, solitary drift.

songs.title: I Can't Go for That (No Can Do)
songs.rationale: An economical synthetic groove and cool boundary-setting contrast with open-ended tenderness.

songs.title: Summer Breeze
songs.rationale: Unhurried acoustic atmosphere and a sense of place invite escape rather than spectacle or command.

pairings.phrase: Studio chrome, or open water with no shore in sight?
pairings.why: Peg rewards precise ensemble propulsion; Sailing drifts into patient, private atmosphere.

pairings.phrase: The studio band punches in, or the narrator disappears after hours?
pairings.why: Rosanna drives a large, assured chorus; Deacon Blues sits alone inside an elaborate, vulnerable account.

pairings.phrase: Dance around the heartbreak, or say you need them back?
pairings.why: The Doobie Brothers keep romantic denial buoyant; Player exposes a slower, less confident plea.

pairings.phrase: Bassline with a grudge, or harmonies that let yesterday breathe?
pairings.why: Michael McDonald's groove insists on the present; Little River Band rewards a gentler, longer memory.

pairings.phrase: Call somebody out, or tell somebody they're the whole world?
pairings.why: Lowdown watches and judges with swagger; Biggest Part of Me offers open reassurance.

pairings.phrase: Let the pocket hypnotize you, or make the big declaration?
pairings.why: Toto invites patient close listening; Kenny Loggins turns soft rock into a more commanding statement.

pairings.phrase: Kick the door open smiling, or vanish behind the horizon?
pairings.why: Hall & Oates make pleasure instant and public; Christopher Cross makes pleasure weightless and solitary.

pairings.phrase: Set a boundary in velvet, or let the whole day drift by?
pairings.why: Hall & Oates keep a polished beat and a firm stance; Seals & Crofts choose easy atmosphere.

pairings.phrase: The lonely genius at closing time, or the couple replaying their favorite night?
pairings.why: Deacon Blues observes alienation from within; Reminiscing keeps a warmer, more shared memory.

pairings.phrase: Perfectly cut edges, or a groove that refuses to hurry?
pairings.why: Peg presents crisp observation and control; Georgy Porgy settles into an intimate, more vulnerable pocket.
